morning.intro: Hello, {name}! It's hungry, chilly and a bit scared. Help it get ready for the day.

afternoon.intro: Tonight your family will knock on your door, and {name} gets scared of knocks. Search the dragon-care websites, and check each one before you trust it: remember Aunt June's warning about Crane's fake websites!

morning.intro: Day 2. Brrr! {name} is shivering: its belly fire went out in the night. Time for breakfast and the spice tin.

intro: Another evening at home. {name} is curled up in the nest, warm from today's spice mix.
Family may stop by again. Help {name} stay calm when you hear footsteps, and remember: you can always show your family the dragon.
Keep watching the window. Crane's helpers have been seen on your street.

morning.intro: Day 3. Whoa, {name} had a growth spurt overnight! It needs a bigger spice mix today. And... is that one of Kit's slippers in the nest?

afternoon.intro: {name} keeps waking up in the night. Find out how to help a hatchling sleep, and check every website carefully: Crane's fake sites might be waiting.

intro: The last evening of the week. {name} is bigger now, and a little restless.
Lots might happen at once tonight. If it does, take a breath: one stone at a time.
As always, you can show your family the dragon, and watch the window for Crane's helpers.

morning.intro: Day 4. {name} is a fledgling now: bigger, stronger, and much too big for the shoebox. Today it moves into the treehouse. Build it a warm nest, then get it ready for the day.

intro: The first night in the treehouse. Everything is new: the creaky boards, the wind, an owl somewhere.
Help {name} feel at home. And keep the lantern low: a bright window shows from the street, and Crane's helpers are still around.

morning.intro: Day 5. {name}'s wings are twitching. Today is flight practice at dawn, behind the hedge where no one can see.

afternoon.intro: Find out how fledglings learn to fly safely. Watch out: the posters pointed to a 'rescue' website. Check it carefully, and see what the library says about the REAL wildlife rescue.

intro: {name} is tired from all that flying. BLINK has been seen patrolling at night with a searchlight.
Keep the treehouse cozy and dark, and watch the window.

morning.intro: Day 6. {name}'s inner fire is getting stronger. Today Aunt June teaches fire control, outdoors on her stone slab.

afternoon.intro: Ms. Ortiz shows you the library's newspaper archive. What do the old newspapers say about Silas Crane?

intro: Something feels different tonight. A car has been parked down the street for an hour.
Stay calm, keep watching, and remember: your family is on your side.

morning.intro: Day 7. Big day! Tonight is the neighborhood meeting. First, a calm morning: you know {name}'s routine by heart now.

intro: A peaceful evening at last. No posters, no clipboards, no red lights sneaking around.
BLINK hums happily on the treehouse windowsill, keeping watch.

morning.intro: Day 8. {name} is restless and keeps staring north. Aunt June comes over with something to show you.

intro: Dusk on Larkspur Hill. Tonight is {name}'s longest flight yet, with BLINK as lookout.
The whole Keeper Circle has come to watch.

morning.intro: Day 9. The last morning of the week. Make it a special one for {name}.

intro: Sunset. Everyone is gathering on Larkspur Hill.

cliffhanger.title: Too big for the shoebox!
paragraphs: That night, {name} turns around three times in the nest... and the shoebox goes CRUNCH. Your dragon has outgrown it!
Aunt June peeks in the next morning and laughs. "Time to think bigger, my dear."
cliffhanger.toldParents: "Your mom and dad already know, so let's have a family meeting about the treehouse."
cliffhanger.notToldParents: "And it's time to talk to your mom and dad. A dragon this size needs the whole family. I'll come with you when you tell them."

cliffhanger.title: Many wings, far away
paragraphs: That night {name} can't settle. It sends you a new kind of thought: tall mountains, and many wings, far away, calling.
Aunt June looks at the sky for a long time. "I've seen that one before," she says quietly. "Tomorrow, we have work to do."
